name: Mohammad Amin Raeisi
location: 512 Arthur K. Watson Hall, 51 Prospect Street, New Haven, CT 06511
description: Mohammad Amin Raeisi is a Computer Science Ph.D. student at Yale working on cryptography, security, and trustworthy AI.
intro: I study cryptography and security, with a particular interest in making AI systems private, verifiable, and trustworthy.
bio: Dorood! I’m Amin, a Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Yale University, working on cryptography and security. I’m very fortunate to be advised by [Babis Papamanthou](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/cpap/).

I’m especially interested in proof systems and cryptographic tools, and I’m enthusiastic about exploring where cryptography and security meet the challenges of LLMs (surprise!). In my free academic time, I enjoy learning about the latest developments in machine learning, the security concerns they raise, and how tools from cryptography and security might help address them. I previously worked on algorithms and theory, before the LLM era changed everything.

Before joining Yale, I earned my B.Sc. in Computer Science at [Sharif University of Technology](https://en.sharif.edu/) and worked with researchers at EPFL, UC Davis, and the University of Maryland during my research explorations.

I’m always eager to connect and talk about cryptography, AI security, and safety. I’d love to explore potential collaborations and, more importantly, get to know people who share these interests and have good conversations. Please feel free to reach out!

interests.title: Cryptography
interests.text: Proof systems, post-quantum cryptography, and cryptography for AI.

interests.title: Trustworthy AI
interests.text: Private and verifiable inference, LLM safety, and verifiable machine learning.

interests.title: Algorithms & systems
interests.text: Parallel and streaming graph algorithms, and secure, usable systems.

teaching.text: Cryptography, algorithms, data structures, automata theory, game theory, linear algebra, probability, and programming.
Taught algorithms, data structures, and competitive programming to around 40 students preparing for the International Olympiad in Informatics.

service.title: Conference reviewing
service.text: Sub-reviewer for ACM CCS 2026, IACR ASIACRYPT 2026, and IACR EUROCRYPT 2027.

service.title: Informatics Olympiad

misc.title: A background in competitive programming
